title: One Input-Length Counting Round
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and let $d$ be a one-work-tape configuration on input $x$, with natural numbers $n,p$ and a Boolean list $v$. Suppose $d$ is in phase count, its input head is at position $n+1$, $n<|x|$, the binary digits of $n$ have either the form of $p$ ones followed by a zero and then $v$, or $p$ ones with $v$ empty, and the binary digits of $n+1$ are $p$ zeros followed by a one and then $v$. Suppose also that the work tape agrees with the buffer tape for the binary digits of $n$ at every offset from the work-head position between $-1$ and the number of binary digits of $n$. After $2p+3$ steps, the machine is in phase count with the binary digits of $n+1$ stored over a segment of length $p+1$, the input head moved by one clamped step to the right, and the work head left at its original position. At each time $u\le 2p+3$, the work-head position is between one cell left of its initial position and its initial position plus $p$.
hypotheses_covered: stated binary digit forms for $n$ and $n+1$
work tape agrees with the buffer for the binary digits of $n$ at offsets $-1$ through its digit length
